title: The deeper secret of the copula
summary: The copula だ / です is a one-way equals sign that puts something in a set. It is not the verb of being: ある says something exists.

blocks.text: You have used だ and です since lesson 1. Here is what they really do. The **copula** is a **one-way equals sign**: A is B, but B is not necessarily A. It places things in **sets**, the most basic way humans think about the world.
さくらは日本人だ says that Sakura belongs to the set of Japanese people. It does not say that every Japanese person is Sakura, so the sign only works in one direction.

blocks.en: Sakura is a Japanese person. (she belongs to the set)

blocks.text: Sets can sit inside bigger sets, and each だ steps one level up.
バラは花だ。花は植物だ。植物は生き物だ。 Each set sits inside the next one, never the other way round.
If the set has only one member, the sign works in both directions. There is only one Sakura, so the two sides are the same thing.

blocks.en: That person is Sakura. (a set of one)

rows: Sakura is inside the bigger set
It says every Japanese person is Sakura

blocks.text: Not the same as ある

English uses one verb, **be**, for two jobs: the copula (I am an American) and **existence** (I think, therefore I am). Spanish separates them (ser / estar versus haber), and so does Japanese: **だ / です** is the copula, **ある / いる** says something exists. Mixing the two causes a lot of confusion.

blocks.en: This is a book. (it belongs to the set "book")
There is a book on the desk. (it exists)

blocks.text: On a train, noun + です is one engine. With ある, the noun is the main carriage and ある is the engine all by itself.
私は学生です。 Noun + copula is one engine.
机の上に本がある。 With ある, the noun is the carriage.

The course treats だ and です as the **same copula**; です is the polite version with one eccentricity. Any logical sentence ends in a verb, an adjective, or a noun plus the copula: a noun cannot end a logical sentence by itself.
The eccentricity: after an い-adjective, です adds no copula at all. かわいい already carries "is", so です only makes it polite (lesson 17).

blocks.jp: この猫はかわいいです。
blocks.en: This cat is cute. (です only adds politeness)

items: The copula is a one-way equals sign: A belongs to set B.
It is not the verb of existence: that is ある / いる.
A logical sentence ends in a verb, an adjective, or noun + copula.
だ and です are one copula in two speech styles.

questions.note: あれは犬です: A belongs to the set B, with です.
The copula says what A is.

questions.prompt: 「学生は田中さんだ」と「田中さんは学生だ」
options: The first says every student is Tanaka
questions.note: The sign goes one way: 田中さんは学生だ is fine, but there are many students.
questions.en: "Students are Tanaka" and "Tanaka is a student"

questions.prompt: A noun can end a logical sentence by itself.
questions.note: A noun is not an engine: it needs the copula.
A is B, but B is not necessarily A.

options: Tanaka belongs to the set of students
questions.note: The copula places Tanaka in a set.

questions.instruction: In which sentence does です add only politeness?
questions.note: After an い-adjective the い already carries "is"; です just makes it polite.

questions.instruction: When does the equals sign work both ways?
options: When the set has only one member
questions.note: あの人はさくらだ works both ways because there is one Sakura.

options: かばんの中にペンがある
questions.note: ある says that a thing exists.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun that です turns into an engine
questions.note: 小学生 + です is one engine.
questions.en: My younger brother is an elementary school student.

questions.note: 机が is the carriage; ある says it exists.
questions.en: There is a big desk in the room.

questions.note: Noun + copula makes the engine.

questions.prompt: There is a cat under the table.
questions.note: いる says a living thing exists.
questions.en: There is a cat under the table.

questions.note: A dog exists: いる, not the copula.
questions.en: There is a dog in the garden.

questions.prompt: 「田中さんは学生だ」 means that all students are Tanaka.
questions.note: The copula goes one way: Tanaka belongs to the set of students.

questions.instruction: English be does two jobs. Which job does ある do?
questions.note: ある / いる say that something exists.

questions.instruction: What is the relationship between だ and です?
options: The same copula in two speech styles
だ is a verb of existence
questions.note: です is the polite copula.

questions.instruction: Which can end a logical sentence?
questions.note: A noun needs the copula to be an engine.

questions.instruction: Which sentence wrongly mixes the copula and existence?
questions.note: がです is wrong: existence takes ある / いる.

questions.prompt: My older sister was a student.
questions.note: Noun + だった is one engine in the past.
questions.en: My older sister was a student.

questions.instruction: Which sentence claims too much, as if every flower were a rose?
questions.note: 花 is the bigger set, so 花はバラだ goes the wrong way.

questions.instruction: What does です add here?
questions.note: The い of かわいい already carries "is".
A set of one: the copula says who that person is.
